title: Food delivery robot makers Coco and Serve hit with biometric privacy lawsuits in Chicago
key_facts: Two lawsuits filed in Cook County claim some food-delivery robots collect hand and facial data without a customer's consent.
The suits allege the robots scan the faces, hands and bodies of customers and of people on the sidewalk.
The companies named are Coco Robotics and Serve Robotics.
Serve says its robots use cameras and sensors to navigate and that it does not use that data to identify individuals.
Coco says it has not collected biometric data in Chicago and has never used lidar there; it calls the suit frivolous.
Carl Hansen, head of government relations at Coco, said the suit misunderstands its technology.
quote_evidence: Two lawsuits filed in Cook County claim that some food delivery robots collect hand and facial data, without a customer's consent.
Serve told ABC7 its robots use cameras and sensors to navigate Chicago sidewalks.
Coco Robotics says it has not collected biometric data in Chicago.
why_it_matters_hint: Illinois has strict biometric privacy rules; delivery robots roam public sidewalks.
notes: Allegations in a lawsuit; both companies deny. The article does not give the filing date or the law cited.
